验证结果：内核模块通过信号向用户态进程推送了 int 值 1234，异步通知机制正常。

---

inotify 和 fanotify 是内核内置的文件系统事件监控子系统。用户态通过系统调用（inotify_init() / fanotify_init()）创建监控实例，通过 inotify_add_watch() / fanotify_mark() 注册监控目标，内核 VFS 层在文件操作发生时将事件写入 fd 对应的内核缓冲区，用户态 read() 读取。不需要自定义内核模块——通信管道由内核提供。

09-inotify和fanotify/
├── inotify_example.c   # inotify 监控程序
└── fanotify_example.c  # fanotify 监控程序

inotify：

fd = inotify_init();                      /* 创建 inotify 实例 */

/* 监控 /tmp 下的创建、删除、修改事件 */
wd = inotify_add_watch(fd, "/tmp", IN_CREATE | IN_DELETE | IN_MODIFY);

/* 阻塞读取事件 */
while ((length = read(fd, buffer, EVENT_BUF_LEN)) > 0) {
    struct inotify_event *event = (struct inotify_event *)&buffer[i];
    if (event->mask & IN_CREATE)
        printf("The file %s was created.\n", event->name);
    if (event->mask & IN_DELETE)
        printf("The file %s was deleted.\n", event->name);
    if (event->mask & IN_MODIFY)
        printf("The file %s was modified.\n", event->name);
}

fanotify：

/* FAN_CLASS_NOTIF: 仅通知，不阻止操作；O_RDONLY: 只读 */
fanotify_fd = fanotify_init(FAN_CLOEXEC | FAN_CLASS_NOTIF, O_RDONLY);

/* 监控 /tmp 挂载点下所有文件的打开和关闭 */
fanotify_mark(fanotify_fd, FAN_MARK_ADD | FAN_MARK_MOUNT,
              FAN_OPEN | FAN_CLOSE, AT_FDCWD, "/tmp");

/* poll 等待 + read 读取事件 */
while (poll(fds, 1, -1) > 0) {
    length = read(fanotify_fd, buffer, EVENT_BUF_LEN);
    /* 遍历事件 */
}
  • inotify 适合监控指定目录/文件的具体事件，轻量易用
  • fanotify 可以监控整个挂载点，支持更多事件类型（需 root 权限）

inotify

inotify_init()

int inotify_init(void);
  • 创建 inotify 实例，返回文件描述符。之后用 read(fd, ...) 读取事件

inotify_add_watch(fd, path, mask)

int inotify_add_watch(int fd, const char *pathname, uint32_t mask);
  • pathname：要监控的目录或文件路径
  • mask：事件类型位掩码，OR 组合 IN_CREATE | IN_DELETE | IN_MODIFY 等
  • 返回 watch descriptor（wd），用于 inotify_rm_watch

inotify_rm_watch(fd, wd) — 移除一个监控目标

fanotify

  • flags=FAN_CLOEXEC|FAN_CLASS_NOTIF：自动 close-on-exec + 仅通知模式（不阻止操作）
  • 返回的文件描述符用 read() 读取事件，建议搭配 poll() 使用

int fanotify_mark(int fanotify_fd, unsigned int flags, uint64_t mask,
                  int dirfd, const char *pathname);
  • flags=FAN_MARK_ADD|FAN_MARK_MOUNT：添加监控整个挂载点
  • mask=FAN_OPEN|FAN_CLOSE：监控文件打开和关闭事件
  • dirfd=AT_FDCWD：路径相对于当前工作目录

用户态                                       内核态（VFS）
─────                                       ─────
fd = inotify_init()          ──► 创建 inotify 实例
wd = inotify_add_watch("/tmp", IN_CREATE|IN_DELETE|IN_MODIFY)
                                    │→ 注册监控 /tmp
read(fd, buf) 阻塞等待               │
      ▲                             │  用户 touch /tmp/xxx
      │  inotify_event              │  内核检测到 IN_CREATE
      │◄─────────────────────────── ┘  写入事件到 fd 缓冲区
      │
      │  打印: "The file xxx was created."
      ▼
read(fd, buf) 阻塞等待下一批事件...

【终端1 - 运行监控程序】

#define _POSIX_C_SOURCE 200809L

#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <unistd.h>

/*
 * PROGRAM:     Named Pipe (FIFO) Reader
 * MECHANISM:   POSIX named pipe / FIFO (mkfifo() filesystem node + open/read)
 * DESCRIPTION: The READER half of an independent two-process FIFO demo.
 *              Creates a FIFO special file at /tmp/ipc_fifo_demo, opens it for
 *              reading (blocks in open() until the writer opens the same path
 *              for writing), reads the byte stream until EOF, prints it, then
 *              removes the FIFO from the filesystem before exiting.  The
 *              reader owns the FIFO lifecycle: it creates the node on startup
 *              and unlinks it on cleanup.
 * USAGE:       1. Start THIS reader first (creates the FIFO):
 *                  ./fifo_reader
 *              2. In another terminal, start the writer program:
 *                  ./fifo_writer
 *              Both programs terminate after a single message exchange.
 * STEPS:       ① Create (or validate) the FIFO special file via mkfifo()
 *              ② Open FIFO for reading (blocks until writer also opens it)
 *              ③ Loop read() until EOF; detect overflow if msg exceeds buffer
 *              ④ Print the message, close fd, unlink() the FIFO path, return
 */

#define FIFO_PATH   "/tmp/ipc_fifo_demo"  /* filesystem path of our FIFO node  */
#define BUFFER_SIZE 256                   /* max bytes we can accept + NUL    */

/*
 * close_checked — close a file descriptor and report errors via perror().
 *
 * close() is NOT retried after EINTR on Linux (the fd is already released
 * before the signal, and retrying could close an unrelated, reassigned fd).
 * We simply report an error and return -1; the caller decides whether to
 * treat this as a fatal exit-status failure.
 *
 * Parameters: fd — open file descriptor to close
 * Return:     0 on success, -1 on close failure (message already printed).
 */
static int close_checked(int fd)
{
    if (close(fd) < 0) {
        perror("close");
        return -1;
    }
    return 0;
}

int main(void)
{
    char buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];
    size_t used = 0;                      /* bytes currently placed in buffer */
    int fd = -1;                          /* FIFO read-end file descriptor    */
    int status = EXIT_FAILURE;            /* pessimistic default; set to 0 OK */
    int path_ready = 0;                   /* 1 iff FIFO_PATH exists as FIFO   */
    int result;
    struct stat path_stat;

    /*
     * ① Create the named pipe (FIFO) special file.
     *
     * mkfifo() creates a new filesystem node with type=FIFO at the given
     * path.  If EEXIST is returned (path already present, possibly left
     * over from a previous run that crashed before unlinking), we do NOT
     * blindly reuse it — instead we lstat() the path and verify via
     * S_ISFIFO() that it really is a FIFO.  This prevents a malicious or
     * confused prior run from leaving a regular file/symlink/socket here
     * that we would then mistakenly read from or write to.
     */
    do {
        result = mkfifo(FIFO_PATH, 0600);   /* owner-only read/write perms */
    } while (result < 0 && errno == EINTR);
    if (result < 0) {
        if (errno != EEXIST) {
            perror("mkfifo");
            goto cleanup;
        }
        /* Path exists — confirm it's actually a FIFO, not a regular file. */
        do {
            result = lstat(FIFO_PATH, &path_stat);    /* get path info */
        } while (result < 0 && errno == EINTR);
        if (result < 0) {
            perror("lstat");
            goto cleanup;
        }
        if (!S_ISFIFO(path_stat.st_mode)) {     /* verify FIFO */
            fprintf(stderr, "%s 已存在但不是 FIFO\n", FIFO_PATH);
            goto cleanup;
        }
    }
    path_ready = 1;

    /*
     * ② Open the FIFO for reading.
     *
     * Because FIFOs require both ends to be open before either open()
     * call returns, opening O_RDONLY here will BLOCK until the partner
     * process (fifo_writer) opens the same path with O_WRONLY.  This
     * rendezvous is a deliberate FIFO design feature (you never end up
     * writing into "nothing").
     *
     * Opening with O_RDWR is also possible (bypasses the handshake) but
     * defeats the purpose of demonstrating the normal pipe-like workflow,
     * so we stick to the one-ended open.
     */
    do {
        fd = open(FIFO_PATH, O_RDONLY);
    } while (fd < 0 && errno == EINTR);
    if (fd < 0) {
        perror("open");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ③ Read until the writer closes its end (read() == 0 means EOF).
     *
     * Always keep one byte free at the end for the NUL terminator we will
     * append.  When the buffer fills completely without yet seeing EOF,
     * we drain one extra byte and check whether there is still more data
     * — if so the message was larger than BUFFER_SIZE and we report an
     * error instead of printing a truncated string.
     */
    while (used < sizeof(buffer) - 1) {
        ssize_t count = read(fd, buffer + used, sizeof(buffer) - 1 - used);

        if (count < 0) {
            if (errno == EINTR)
                continue;
            perror("read");
            goto cleanup;
        }
        if (count == 0)
            break;                       /* writer closed → EOF */
        used += (size_t)count;
    }
    if (used == sizeof(buffer) - 1) {
        /* Buffer is full; verify the writer actually ended the message. */
        char extra;
        ssize_t count;

        do {
            count = read(fd, &extra, sizeof(extra));
        } while (count < 0 && errno == EINTR);
        if (count < 0) {
            perror("read");
            goto cleanup;
        }
        if (count > 0) {
            /* More bytes exist — message was larger than we can store. */
            fprintf(stderr, "FIFO 消息超过缓冲区限制\n");
            goto cleanup;
        }
    }
    buffer[used] = '\0';                /* NUL-terminate for printf("%s") */

    if (printf("reader 收到：%s\n", buffer) < 0) {
        perror("printf");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    status = EXIT_SUCCESS;

cleanup:
    /* Close the FIFO fd first; errors here degrade exit status to failure. */
    if (fd >= 0 && close_checked(fd) < 0)
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;

    /*
     * ④ Unlink the FIFO from the filesystem.
     *
     * Since the reader created the FIFO it is also responsible for
     * removing it so /tmp doesn't accumulate leftover special files.
     * We ignore ENOENT (someone else already removed it) but fail for
     * other errors.
     */
    if (path_ready) {
        do {
            result = unlink(FIFO_PATH);
        } while (result < 0 && errno == EINTR);
        if (result < 0 && errno != ENOENT) {
            perror("unlink");
            status = EXIT_FAILURE;
        }
    }
    return status;
}

#define _POSIX_C_SOURCE 200809L

#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

/*
 * PROGRAM:     Named Pipe (FIFO) Writer
 * MECHANISM:   POSIX named pipe / FIFO (mkfifo() filesystem node + open/read)
 * DESCRIPTION: The WRITER half of an independent two-process FIFO demo.
 *              Opens the FIFO path created by fifo_reader, writes a Chinese
 *              greeting message, and closes the write end (which delivers EOF
 *              to the reader so it can stop reading).  Unlike an anonymous
 *              pipe, a FIFO is accessed via a regular filesystem path, so the
 *              two processes can be completely unrelated (different parents,
 *              different terminals, different start times).
 * USAGE:       1. Start the READER first (it creates the FIFO node):
 *                  ./fifo_reader
 *              2. In another terminal, start this writer:
 *                  ./fifo_writer
 *              The writer blocks in open() until the reader has also opened
 *              the FIFO for reading.
 * STEPS:       ① Ignore SIGPIPE so premature reader close yields EPIPE
 *              ② Open the FIFO for writing (blocks until reader also opens)
 *              ③ Write the full message with write_all()
 *              ④ Close the write end → reader sees EOF and terminates
 */

#define FIFO_PATH "/tmp/ipc_fifo_demo"   /* filesystem path of the FIFO node   */

/*
 * write_all — reliably write exactly `length` bytes to a file descriptor.
 *
 * See pipe_demo.c for full documentation; duplicated here to keep each
 * demo file self-contained for teaching purposes.
 *
 * Parameters: fd, buffer, length — see pipe_demo.c
 * Return:     0 on success, -1 on hard error (errno set).
 */
static int write_all(int fd, const void *buffer, size_t length)
{
    const char *cursor = buffer;

    while (length > 0) {
        ssize_t written = write(fd, cursor, length);

        if (written < 0) {
            if (errno == EINTR)
                continue;
            return -1;
        }
        if (written == 0) {
            errno = EIO;
            return -1;
        }
        cursor += (size_t)written;
        length -= (size_t)written;
    }
    return 0;
}

int main(void)
{
    static const char message[] = "你好，reader！这是来自独立 writer 的消息。";
    int fd;
    int status = EXIT_SUCCESS;
    struct sigaction action; /* signal action struct */

    /*
     * Suppress SIGPIPE (default = kill process).
     *
     * If the reader process exits/crashes before we finish writing, the
     * kernel would normally send SIGPIPE to terminate us silently.  Ignoring
     * the signal makes write() return -1 with errno = EPIPE instead, so our
     * normal error path prints a diagnostic via perror("write") and exits
     * with a visible failure status.
     */
    memset(&action, 0, sizeof(action));
    action.sa_handler = SIG_IGN;
    if (sigemptyset(&action.sa_mask) < 0) {
        perror("sigemptyset");
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    if (sigaction(SIGPIPE, &action, NULL) < 0) {
        perror("sigaction");
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    /*
     * ① Open the FIFO that the reader program created at FIFO_PATH.
     *
     * FIFO semantics are symmetric: a process that opens with O_WRONLY
     * blocks inside open() until some other process opens the same path
     * with O_RDONLY (and vice versa).  This handshake guarantees that when
     * open returns, both communication partners are ready.
     *
     * The reader must therefore be started BEFORE the writer, otherwise
     * open() here fails with ENOENT because /tmp/ipc_fifo_demo does not
     * exist yet.
     */
    do {
        fd = open(FIFO_PATH, O_WRONLY);
    } while (fd < 0 && errno == EINTR);
    if (fd < 0) {
        perror("open");
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    /*
     * ② Write the entire message.
     *
     * Do not assume a single write() call delivers every byte — pipe-like
     * objects have finite kernel buffers and can return partial counts when
     * the reader is slow to drain them.  write_all() loops internally.
     */
    if (write_all(fd, message, strlen(message)) < 0) {
        perror("write");
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    /*
     * ③ Close the write end.
     *
     * Closing the last (or only) writer reference is what produces the
     * 0-byte read (EOF) in the reader, telling it that no more data will
     * arrive and it may finish.  If we skipped this step and the writer
     * kept the fd open (e.g. by exiting uncleanly), the reader would hang
     * forever.
     */
    if (close(fd) < 0) {
        perror("close");
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    return status;
}

CFLAGS ?= -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -std=c11 -O2

#define _POSIX_C_SOURCE 200809L   /* enable POSIX features */

#include <errno.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/wait.h>
#include <unistd.h>

/*
 * PROGRAM:     Anonymous Pipe IPC Demo (Parent → Child)
 * MECHANISM:   POSIX anonymous pipe (`pipe()` + `fork()`)
 * DESCRIPTION: Demonstrates one-way communication from a parent process to
 *              its child via an anonymous pipe. The parent writes a Chinese
 *              greeting message; the child reads it and prints it to stdout.
 *              Anonymous pipes require a parent/child (fork-based) relationship
 *              since the pipe file descriptors must be inherited — they have
 *              no name in the filesystem and cannot be opened by unrelated
 *              processes.
 * USAGE:       Compile with:   make pipe_demo   (or `gcc -o pipe_demo pipe_demo.c`)
 *              Run with:       ./pipe_demo
 *              No partner program is needed — both ends live in this single
 *              process image via fork().
 * STEPS:       ① Ignore SIGPIPE so write-end closure yields EPIPE, not kill
 *              ② Create the anonymous pipe (read-end fd[0], write-end fd[1])
 *              ③ Fork; each side closes the end it does NOT use
 *              ④ Child loops read() until EOF, then prints the message
 *              ⑤ Parent writes full message, closes write-end (sends EOF),
 *                waitpid()s for the child, and reports exit status.
 */

#define BUFFER_SIZE 256   /* maximum bytes read by child (incl. NUL terminator) */

/*
 * write_all — reliably write exactly `length` bytes to a file descriptor.
 *
 * The plain write() syscall is permitted to return fewer bytes than requested
 * (partial write) for several reasons: interrupted delivery, kernel buffer
 * pressure, pipe/SOCKET buffer limits, etc.  This helper loops until every
 * byte is accepted or a hard error occurs.
 *
 * Parameters:
 *   fd     — writable file descriptor (pipe write-end, socket, regular file, …)
 *   buffer — pointer to the first byte to write
 *   length — exact number of bytes to transfer from `buffer`
 *
 * Return:  0 on success (all bytes written)
 *          -1 on failure with `errno` set by the failing write() call.
 *          On EINTR (interrupted by a signal) the call is silently retried.
 *          A zero-byte write (should not happen for valid fds) is treated as
 *          an I/O error (errno forced to EIO) because it would otherwise
 *          cause an infinite loop.
 */
static int write_all(int fd, const void *buffer, size_t length)
{
    const char *cursor = buffer;

    while (length > 0) {
        ssize_t written = write(fd, cursor, length);

        if (written < 0) {
            /* POSIX allows write() to be interrupted by a signal before any
             * bytes are transferred; retry transparently. */
            if (errno == EINTR)
                continue;
            return -1;
        }
        if (written == 0) {
            errno = EIO;
            return -1;
        }
        cursor += (size_t)written;  /* update cursor */
        length -= (size_t)written;  /* update length */
    }
    return 0;
}

/*
 * close_checked — close a file descriptor and report errors to stderr.
 *
 * close() is NOT safe to restart after EINTR on many Linux versions (the fd
 * is already deallocated by the time the signal handler returns, so retrying
 * would close an unrelated fd that was reassigned by another thread).  We
 * therefore report the error via perror() and let the caller decide the
 * process exit status — we never loop here.
 *
 * Parameters:
 *   fd — open file descriptor to close
 *
 * Return:  0 on success, -1 if close() failed (error already printed).
 */
static int close_checked(int fd)
{
    if (close(fd) < 0) {
        perror("close");
        return -1;
    }
    return 0;
}

int main(void)
{
    static const char message[] = "你好，子进程！这是来自父进程的消息。";
    int pipefd[2];                 /* [0] = read end, [1] = write end */
    pid_t pid;
    struct sigaction action;

    /*
     * ① Ignore SIGPIPE.
     *
     * By default, writing to a pipe/socket whose read end has been closed
     * causes the kernel to deliver SIGPIPE to the writer — the default
     * action is to kill the process silently.  By setting the handler to
     * SIG_IGN we ask the kernel to instead make write() fail with EPIPE,
     * which lets us run the same error/cleanup path as any other I/O
     * failure and produce a diagnostic message rather than a silent exit.
     */
    memset(&action, 0, sizeof(action));
    action.sa_handler = SIG_IGN;
    if (sigemptyset(&action.sa_mask) < 0) {
        perror("sigemptyset");
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    if (sigaction(SIGPIPE, &action, NULL) < 0) {
        perror("sigaction");
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    /*
     * ② Create the anonymous pipe.
     *
     * pipe() populates a two-element int array:
     *   pipefd[0] — the READ  end (data written to [1] comes out here)
     *   pipefd[1] — the WRITE end
     *
     * Data is a simple byte stream with no message boundaries (same
     * semantics as SOCK_STREAM); the kernel buffers up to PIPE_BUF bytes
     * internally.  Anonymous pipes only exist inside this process and
     * descendants that inherit the fds across fork().
     */
    if (pipe(pipefd) < 0) {
        perror("pipe");
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    /*
     * ③ Fork the child process.
     *
     * After fork() BOTH parent and child hold references to BOTH pipe ends.
     * The reader will never see EOF as long as ANY write-end reference is
     * still open anywhere, so each side MUST close the end it won't use:
     *   • child  → closes write-end, keeps read-end
     *   • parent → closes read-end,  keeps write-end
     *
     * If fork() fails we close both ends before returning to avoid fd leaks.
     */
    pid = fork();
    if (pid < 0) {
        perror("fork");
        (void)close_checked(pipefd[0]);
        (void)close_checked(pipefd[1]);
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    if (pid == 0) {
        /* ------------------------------ CHILD ------------------------------ */
        char buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];
        size_t used = 0;                   /* bytes currently in buffer[]     */
        int status = EXIT_SUCCESS;

        /* Child will only read, so the inherited write end is closed now. */
        if (close_checked(pipefd[1]) < 0)
            status = EXIT_FAILURE;

        /*
         * ④ Child reads the pipe until EOF (read returns 0).
         *
         * One slot at the end of buffer[] is ALWAYS reserved for the NUL
         * terminator we append after the loop, so the read-capacity is
         * sizeof(buffer) - 1.  read() blocks when no data is available and
         * the write end is still open somewhere; once the parent closes
         * its write-end reference, the next read() with an empty buffer
         * returns 0 (EOF).
         */
        while (status == EXIT_SUCCESS && used < sizeof(buffer) - 1) {
            ssize_t count = read(pipefd[0], buffer + used,
                                 sizeof(buffer) - 1 - used);

            if (count < 0) {
                /* Interrupted by a signal — retry with the same parameters. */
                if (errno == EINTR)
                    continue;
                perror("read");
                status = EXIT_FAILURE;
                break;
            }
            if (count == 0)
                break;              /* EOF: parent closed the write end */
            used += (size_t)count;
        }
        buffer[used] = '\0';          /* NUL-terminate for printf("%s") */

        if (status == EXIT_SUCCESS &&
            printf("子进程收到：%s\n", buffer) < 0) {
            perror("printf");
            status = EXIT_FAILURE;
        }
        if (close_checked(pipefd[0]) < 0)
            status = EXIT_FAILURE;
        exit(status);                /* Child terminates; DO NOT fall through */
    }

    /* ------------------------------ PARENT ------------------------------ */
    /*
     * ⑤ Parent closes the read end, writes the message, closes the write
     *    end (which sends EOF to the child), then reaps the child with
     *    waitpid() and propagates its exit status.
     */
    {
        int status = EXIT_SUCCESS;
        int child_status;

        /* Parent will only write, so inherited read end is closed now. */
        if (close_checked(pipefd[0]) < 0)
            status = EXIT_FAILURE;
        if (write_all(pipefd[1], message, strlen(message)) < 0) {
            perror("write");
            status = EXIT_FAILURE;
        }
        /* Closing write-end is how the child learns there is no more data. */
        if (close_checked(pipefd[1]) < 0)
            status = EXIT_FAILURE;

        /* waitpid() may be interrupted — retry on EINTR. */
        do {
            pid = waitpid(pid, &child_status, 0);
        } while (pid < 0 && errno == EINTR);
        if (pid < 0) {
            perror("waitpid");
            return EXIT_FAILURE;
        }
        /* Consider the whole run a failure if the child crashed or errored. */
        if (!WIFEXITED(child_status) ||
            WEXITSTATUS(child_status) != EXIT_SUCCESS)
            status = EXIT_FAILURE;
        return status;
    }
}

#include <errno.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <sys/un.h>   /* sockaddr_un */
#include <unistd.h>

/*
 * PROGRAM:     UNIX Domain Socket Client (SOCK_STREAM)
 * MECHANISM:   POSIX UNIX domain stream socket (AF_UNIX + SOCK_STREAM)
 * DESCRIPTION: The CLIENT half of a local request/reply pair.  Creates an
 *              AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM socket, connect()s to the path
 *              /tmp/ipc_unix_demo.sock (created by unix_server), sends a
 *              NUL-terminated Chinese greeting, then waits for and prints
 *              the server's reply.
 * USAGE:       1. Start the server first (it binds the socket path):
 *                  ./unix_server
 *              2. In another terminal run this client:
 *                  ./unix_client
 * STEPS:       ① Create AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM socket
 *              ② Fill sockaddr_un with server's path and connect()
 *              ③ Send NUL-framed request (sizeof includes NUL)
 *              ④ Receive NUL-framed reply and print it
 *              ⑤ close() socket and return exit status
 */

#define SOCKET_PATH "/tmp/ipc_unix_demo.sock"  /* server's bind path          */
#define BUFFER_SIZE 256                        /* max reply size + NUL        */

/*
 * send_all — stream-socket exact-byte send helper.
 * See unix_server.c /receive_string and send_all comment blocks for full doc.
 */
static int send_all(int fd, const void *buffer, size_t length)
{
    const char *cursor = buffer;

    while (length > 0) {
        ssize_t sent = send(fd, cursor, length, MSG_NOSIGNAL);    /*MSG_NOSIGNAL: don't send SIGPIPE */

        if (sent < 0) {
            if (errno == EINTR)
                continue;
            return -1;
        }
        if (sent == 0) {
            errno = EPIPE;
            return -1;
        }
        cursor += (size_t)sent;
        length -= (size_t)sent;
    }
    return 0;
}

/*
 * receive_string — read one NUL-delimited string from a stream socket.
 * See unix_server.c for full documentation.
 */
static int receive_string(int fd, char *buffer, size_t capacity)
{
    size_t used = 0;

    while (used < capacity) {
        ssize_t count = recv(fd, buffer + used, capacity - used, 0);

        if (count < 0) {
            if (errno == EINTR)
                continue;
            return -1;
        }
        if (count == 0) {       /* server closed connection */
            errno = EPROTO;
            return -1;
        }
        if (memchr(buffer + used, '\0', (size_t)count) != NULL)     /* search for NUL */
            return 0;
        used += (size_t)count;
    }
    buffer[capacity - 1] = '\0';
    errno = EMSGSIZE;     /* buffer overflow */
    return -1;
}

int main(void)
{
    static const char request[] = "你好，UNIX server！";
    struct sockaddr_un address;          /* AF_UNIX address → pathname       */
    char response[BUFFER_SIZE];          /* server's reply buffer            */
    int fd;                              /* client socket fd                 */
    int status = EXIT_FAILURE;           /* pessimistic default              */
    int result;

    /*
     * ① Create the AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM socket.
     *
     * No bind() is needed on the client side for SOCK_STREAM UNIX sockets
     * in the common case: the kernel picks an ephemeral address (or, for
     * Linux pathname sockets, simply leaves it unnamed).  Only servers
     * that need to accept() connections must bind to a known address.
     */
    fd = socket(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
    if (fd < 0) {
        perror("socket");
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    memset(&address, 0, sizeof(address));
    address.sun_family = AF_UNIX;
    result = snprintf(address.sun_path, sizeof(address.sun_path), "%s",
                      SOCKET_PATH);
    if (result < 0 || result >= (int)sizeof(address.sun_path)) {
        fprintf(stderr, "socket 路径过长\n");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ② Connect to the server's socket path.
     *
     * connect() on AF_UNIX performs a rendezvous with the server's
     * listen()+accept() state machine: if the backlog is full it blocks,
     * if the path doesn't exist it fails with ENOENT.  As with all slow
     * syscalls, EINTR must be retried.
     */
    do {
        result = connect(fd, (struct sockaddr *)&address, sizeof(address));
    } while (result < 0 && errno == EINTR);
    if (result < 0) {
        perror("connect");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ③ Send the request, wait for the reply, print.
     *
     * sizeof(request) is passed (not strlen) because the trailing '\0'
     * byte acts as our NUL-delimiter message boundary in the byte stream.
     * receive_string() on the server side scans for that exact NUL to
     * know when one request is complete.
     */
    if (send_all(fd, request, sizeof(request)) < 0) {
        perror("send");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    if (receive_string(fd, response, sizeof(response)) < 0) {
        perror("recv");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    if (printf("client 收到：%s\n", response) < 0) {
        perror("printf");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    status = EXIT_SUCCESS;

cleanup:
    if (close(fd) < 0) {
        perror("close");
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    return status;
}

#define _POSIX_C_SOURCE 200809L

#include <errno.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <sys/un.h>
#include <unistd.h>

/*
 * PROGRAM:     UNIX Domain Socket Server (SOCK_STREAM)
 * MECHANISM:   POSIX UNIX domain stream socket (AF_UNIX + SOCK_STREAM,
 *              filesystem-backed pathname socket)
 * DESCRIPTION: The SERVER half of a local request/reply pair.  Creates an
 *              AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM socket bound to /tmp/ipc_unix_demo.sock,
 *              listens for exactly one connection, reads a NUL-terminated
 *              request string, prints it, and writes a fixed reply string.
 *              UNIX domain sockets only work between processes on the SAME
 *              host kernel (they have no network layer), but enjoy lower
 *              overhead and richer ancillary-data capabilities than TCP.
 * USAGE:       1. Start the server first (it creates the socket path):
 *                  ./unix_server
 *              2. In another terminal run the client:
 *                  ./unix_client
 *              Server handles one client then exits and removes the socket.
 * STEPS:       ① Verify/remove stale socket path at SOCKET_PATH
 *              ② Create AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM socket, bind to path, listen(1)
 *              ③ accept() one client (blocks until unix_client connects)
 *              ④ Receive one NUL-delimited request, print, send reply
 *              ⑤ Close fds and unlink() the socket path from the filesystem
 */

#define SOCKET_PATH "/tmp/ipc_unix_demo.sock"  /* socket inode path (≤108 chars) */
#define BUFFER_SIZE 256                        /* max framed msg size + NUL    */

/*
 * send_all — send exactly `length` bytes on a connected stream socket.
 *
 * send() on a SOCK_STREAM socket behaves exactly like write() for our
 * purposes: it may deliver fewer bytes than requested due to kernel
 * transmit-buffer exhaustion.  This helper loops until all bytes are
 * accepted.
 *
 * Parameters:
 *   fd     — connected, writable stream-socket file descriptor
 *   buffer — start of bytes to send
 *   length — number of bytes to transfer
 *
 * Return: 0 on success (all bytes handed to the kernel for transmission).
 *        -1 on hard failure with errno set by the failing send().
 * Special:
 *   - MSG_NOSIGNAL is passed so a premature peer close returns EPIPE
 *     instead of delivering SIGPIPE (which would kill us by default).
 *   - EINTR is silently retried.
 *   - A zero-byte send (should never happen for connected sockets) is
 *     treated as EPIPE (peer already closed).
 */
static int send_all(int fd, const void *buffer, size_t length)
{
    const char *cursor = buffer;

    while (length > 0) {
        ssize_t sent = send(fd, cursor, length, MSG_NOSIGNAL);

        if (sent < 0) {
            if (errno == EINTR)
                continue;
            return -1;
        }
        if (sent == 0) {
            errno = EPIPE;
            return -1;
        }
        cursor += (size_t)sent;
        length -= (size_t)sent;
    }
    return 0;
}

/*
 * receive_string — receive one NUL-terminated string on a stream socket.
 *
 * STREAM sockets (SOCK_STREAM, TCP, UNIX) deliver an opaque BYTE STREAM
 * with NO built-in message boundaries.  This demo protocol uses the NUL
 * byte ('\0') as an in-band delimiter — identical to C string framing.
 * The helper recv()s until either a NUL is found within the received
 * window (success) or the buffer would overflow.
 *
 * Parameters:
 *   fd       — connected, readable stream-socket file descriptor
 *   buffer   — destination array; at most `capacity` bytes are written
 *   capacity — total size of `buffer` in bytes (including NUL room)
 *
 * Return:  0 on success; buffer[] holds a valid NUL-terminated C string.
 *         -1 on failure with errno set:
 *              EINTR   → retried internally
 *              EPROTO  → peer sent FIN/EOF before terminating NUL
 *              EMSGSIZE→ message exceeded capacity-1 without NUL
 *              other   → recv() error
 */
static int receive_string(int fd, char *buffer, size_t capacity)
{
    size_t used = 0;

    while (used < capacity) {
        ssize_t count = recv(fd, buffer + used, capacity - used, 0);

        if (count < 0) {
            if (errno == EINTR)
                continue;
            return -1;
        }
        if (count == 0) {
            /* Peer closed before sending NUL terminator — protocol error. */
            errno = EPROTO;
            return -1;
        }
        /* Did the most recent chunk contain the NUL delimiter?  If so we
         * have a complete message and can return immediately. */
        if (memchr(buffer + used, '\0', (size_t)count) != NULL)
            return 0;
        used += (size_t)count;
    }
    /* Buffer full with no NUL found → message too long. */
    buffer[capacity - 1] = '\0';
    errno = EMSGSIZE;
    return -1;
}

/*
 * close_checked — close a fd, print error to stderr; see pipe_demo.c.
 */
static int close_checked(int fd)
{
    if (close(fd) < 0) {
        perror("close");
        return -1;
    }
    return 0;
}

/*
 * remove_socket_path — unlink() the socket file, ignoring ENOENT.
 *
 * On EINTR the syscall is retried (unlink is "fast" but POSIX still allows
 * signal interruption in certain implementations).  Any other errno besides
 * ENOENT is reported via perror and returns -1.
 */
static int remove_socket_path(void)
{
    int result;

    do {
        result = unlink(SOCKET_PATH);
    } while (result < 0 && errno == EINTR);
    if (result < 0 && errno != ENOENT) {
        perror("unlink");
        return -1;
    }
    return 0;
}

int main(void)
{
    static const char response[] = "server 已收到 UNIX 域套接字请求";
    struct sockaddr_un address;          /* AF_UNIX pathname address struct  */
    struct stat path_stat;               /* for verifying stale path type    */
    char request[BUFFER_SIZE];           /* holds client request (NUL-term)  */
    int listen_fd = -1;                  /* listening (passive) socket fd    */
    int client_fd = -1;                  /* accepted (active) client fd      */
    int status = EXIT_FAILURE;           /* pessimistic; flipped at the end  */
    int path_bound = 0;                  /* 1 once bind() has succeeded      */
    int result;

    /*
     * ① Clean up any leftover socket file from a prior crashed run.
     *
     * bind(AF_UNIX) fails with EADDRINUSE if the filesystem path already
     * exists, even if no process currently holds a socket bound to it.
     * Before blindly unlinking, we lstat() and check S_ISSOCK() — refusing
     * to delete a regular file, directory, or symlink that happened to
     * share our path.  If the path does not exist (ENOENT) that is fine;
     * we just proceed to create a fresh one.
     */
    do {
        result = lstat(SOCKET_PATH, &path_stat);
    } while (result < 0 && errno == EINTR);
    if (result == 0) {
        if (!S_ISSOCK(path_stat.st_mode)) {
            fprintf(stderr, "%s 已存在但不是 socket\n", SOCKET_PATH);
            goto cleanup;
        }
        if (remove_socket_path() < 0)
            goto cleanup;
    } else if (errno != ENOENT) {
        perror("lstat");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ② Create, bind, and listen on the AF_UNIX socket.
     *
     * struct sockaddr_un only provides 108 bytes for sun_path on Linux,
     * so we snprintf() the path and verify it fits before bind().  Using
     * a pathname socket (rather than Linux's abstract namespace) keeps the
     * demo portable: any POSIX system supports pathname UNIX sockets, and
     * the visible file makes it easier to understand what bind() creates.
     */
    listen_fd = socket(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, 0);      /* domain: AF_UNIX, type: SOCK_STREAM, protocol: 0 */
    if (listen_fd < 0) {
        perror("socket");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    memset(&address, 0, sizeof(address));
    address.sun_family = AF_UNIX;
    result = snprintf(address.sun_path, sizeof(address.sun_path), "%s",
                      SOCKET_PATH);
    if (result < 0 || result >= (int)sizeof(address.sun_path)) {
        fprintf(stderr, "socket 路径过长\n");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    if (bind(listen_fd, (struct sockaddr *)&address, sizeof(address)) < 0) {
        perror("bind");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    path_bound = 1;                      /* remember to unlink on cleanup */
    /* Backlog of 1 is sufficient: the demo serves exactly one client. */
    if (listen(listen_fd, 1) < 0) {
        perror("listen");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ③ Accept exactly one client connection.
     *
     * accept() blocks until unix_client calls connect() on the same path.
     * The sockaddr parameters are NULL because we don't need to know the
     * client's address (all clients are local and there's only one).
     */
    do {
        client_fd = accept(listen_fd, NULL, NULL);
    } while (client_fd < 0 && errno == EINTR);
    if (client_fd < 0) {
        perror("accept");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ④ Protocol: read one NUL-framed request, then send one NUL-framed reply.
     *
     * receive_string/send_all both handle partial-read/partial-write and
     * EINTR internally so the main flow reads as a clean RPC pair.
     */
    if (receive_string(client_fd, request, sizeof(request)) < 0) {
        perror("recv");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    if (printf("server 收到：%s\n", request) < 0) {
        perror("printf");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    /* sizeof(response) includes the trailing '\0' which acts as frame marker. */
    if (send_all(client_fd, response, sizeof(response)) < 0) {
        perror("send");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    status = EXIT_SUCCESS;

cleanup:
    if (client_fd >= 0 && close_checked(client_fd) < 0)
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    if (listen_fd >= 0 && close_checked(listen_fd) < 0)
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    /* Server owns the socket path; remove it so /tmp doesn't leak inodes. */
    if (path_bound && remove_socket_path() < 0)
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    return status;
}

/*
 * PROGRAM:     TCP/IP Loopback Client (IPv4, SOCK_STREAM)
 * MECHANISM:   POSIX TCP socket (AF_INET + SOCK_STREAM) over the loopback
 *              interface 127.0.0.1
 * DESCRIPTION: The CLIENT half of a TCP request/reply demo.  Creates an
 *              IPv4 TCP socket, connect()s to 127.0.0.1:8888 (where
 *              tcp_server is listening), sends a NUL-terminated Chinese
 *              greeting, blocks waiting for the server's NUL-terminated
 *              reply, and prints the reply to stdout.
 * USAGE:       1. Start the TCP server first (it binds port 8888):
 *                  ./tcp_server
 *              2. In another terminal, run this client:
 *                  ./tcp_client
 * STEPS:       ① socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0)
 *              ② Fill sockaddr_in with 127.0.0.1:8888 and connect()
 *              ③ send_all() framed request (sizeof includes NUL)
 *              ④ receive_string() framed reply and print it
 *              ⑤ close() socket, return exit status
 */

#define SERVER_PORT 8888                /* same port tcp_server listens on   */
#define BUFFER_SIZE 256                 /* max reply size + NUL terminator   */

/*
 * send_all — reliably send exactly `length` bytes on a connected stream socket.
 * See unix_server.c → send_all for full semantics.
 */
static int send_all(int fd, const void *buffer, size_t length)
{
    const char *cursor = buffer;

    while (length > 0) {
        ssize_t sent = send(fd, cursor, length, MSG_NOSIGNAL);

        if (sent < 0) {
            if (errno == EINTR)
                continue;
            return -1;
        }
        if (sent == 0) {
            errno = EPIPE;
            return -1;
        }
        cursor += (size_t)sent;
        length -= (size_t)sent;
    }
    return 0;
}

/*
 * receive_string — receive a NUL-delimited string from a SOCK_STREAM socket.
 * See unix_server.c → receive_string for full semantics.
 */
static int receive_string(int fd, char *buffer, size_t capacity)
{
    size_t used = 0;

    while (used < capacity) {
        ssize_t count = recv(fd, buffer + used, capacity - used, 0);

        if (count < 0) {
            if (errno == EINTR)
                continue;
            return -1;
        }
        if (count == 0) {
            errno = EPROTO;
            return -1;
        }
        if (memchr(buffer + used, '\0', (size_t)count) != NULL)
            return 0;
        used += (size_t)count;
    }
    buffer[capacity - 1] = '\0';
    errno = EMSGSIZE;
    return -1;
}

int main(void)
{
    static const char request[] = "你好，TCP server！";
    struct sockaddr_in address;           /* server's IPv4 endpoint           */
    char response[BUFFER_SIZE];           /* server reply goes here           */
    int fd;                               /* client TCP socket fd             */
    int result;
    int status = EXIT_FAILURE;            /* pessimistic until proven OK      */

    /*
     * ① Create an IPv4 TCP (SOCK_STREAM) socket.
     *
     * No explicit bind() is needed on the client: the kernel picks a free
     * ephemeral port in the range ip_local_port_range and binds to it
     * automatically when connect() is called.
     */
    fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
    if (fd < 0) {
        perror("socket");
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    memset(&address, 0, sizeof(address));
    address.sin_family = AF_INET;
    address.sin_port = htons(SERVER_PORT);
    if (inet_pton(AF_INET, "127.0.0.1", &address.sin_addr) != 1) {
        fprintf(stderr, "inet_pton: 无效的 IPv4 地址\n");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ② Initiate the TCP 3-way handshake by calling connect().
     *
     * connect() blocks until:
     *   • The handshake completes (SYN → SYN+ACK → ACK), or
     *   • The connection is refused (ECONNREFUSED — server not listening), or
     *   • A timeout elapses (ETIMEDOUT), or
     *   • A signal interrupts the call (EINTR — retried here).
     */
    do {
        result = connect(fd, (struct sockaddr *)&address, sizeof(address));
    } while (result < 0 && errno == EINTR);
    if (result < 0) {
        perror("connect");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ③ Send one NUL-framed request then wait for / print the reply.
     *
     * sizeof(request) (NOT strlen) is passed because the trailing '\0'
     * byte is part of our simple wire protocol: it tells the server's
     * receive_string() that the request is complete.  The server replies
     * with the same framing convention.
     */
    if (send_all(fd, request, sizeof(request)) < 0) {
        perror("send");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    if (receive_string(fd, response, sizeof(response)) < 0) {
        perror("recv");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    if (printf("client 收到：%s\n", response) < 0) {
        perror("printf");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    status = EXIT_SUCCESS;

cleanup:
    if (close(fd) < 0) {
        perror("close");
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    return status;
}

#include <arpa/inet.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <unistd.h>

/*
 * PROGRAM:     TCP/IP Loopback Server (IPv4, SOCK_STREAM)
 * MECHANISM:   POSIX TCP socket (AF_INET + SOCK_STREAM) over the loopback
 *              interface 127.0.0.1
 * DESCRIPTION: The SERVER half of a TCP request/reply demo.  Creates an
 *              IPv4 TCP socket, enables SO_REUSEADDR to allow fast restart,
 *              binds to 127.0.0.1:8888, listens, accepts one client, reads
 *              a NUL-terminated request, prints it, and sends a fixed
 *              NUL-terminated reply.  Binding to 127.0.0.1 (instead of
 *              INADDR_ANY) intentionally rejects connections from any other
 *              host — keeping this a local-only demo like AF_UNIX.
 * USAGE:       1. Start server first (it binds the port):
 *                  ./tcp_server
 *              2. In another terminal, run the client:
 *                  ./tcp_client
 * STEPS:       ① socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM) + SO_REUSEADDR option
 *              ② bind() 127.0.0.1:8888 (loopback-only), listen(backlog=1)
 *              ③ accept() one client (blocks until tcp_client connects)
 *              ④ receive_string() → print → send_all() reply
 *              ⑤ close both fds, return status
 */

#define SERVER_PORT 8888                 /* TCP port the server listens on  */
#define BUFFER_SIZE 256                  /* max framed msg size + NUL       */

/*
 * send_all — stream-socket exact-byte send helper.
 *
 * See unix_server.c → send_all block for full documentation.
 * Behavior: loops on partial send, retries EINTR, returns EPIPE on 0-byte
 * send or peer-close via MSG_NOSIGNAL.
 */
static int send_all(int fd, const void *buffer, size_t length)
{
    const char *cursor = buffer;

    while (length > 0) {
        ssize_t sent = send(fd, cursor, length, MSG_NOSIGNAL);

        if (sent < 0) {
            if (errno == EINTR)
                continue;
            return -1;
        }
        if (sent == 0) {
            errno = EPIPE;
            return -1;
        }
        cursor += (size_t)sent;
        length -= (size_t)sent;
    }
    return 0;
}

/*
 * receive_string — read one NUL-delimited message from a SOCK_STREAM socket.
 *
 * SOCK_STREAM (TCP) guarantees reliable, in-order delivery of a raw byte
 * stream with NO per-message boundaries.  This demo protocol uses a NUL
 * byte as an in-band delimiter: the helper reads until a '\0' appears in
 * the stream, at which point a complete C string is available in buffer[].
 *
 * See unix_server.c → receive_string for full semantics (EPROTO on early
 * FIN, EMSGSIZE on overflow, EINTR retried).
 */
static int receive_string(int fd, char *buffer, size_t capacity)
{
    size_t used = 0;

    while (used < capacity) {
        ssize_t count = recv(fd, buffer + used, capacity - used, 0);

        if (count < 0) {
            if (errno == EINTR)
                continue;
            return -1;
        }
        if (count == 0) {
            errno = EPROTO;
            return -1;
        }
        if (memchr(buffer + used, '\0', (size_t)count) != NULL)
            return 0;
        used += (size_t)count;
    }
    buffer[capacity - 1] = '\0';
    errno = EMSGSIZE;
    return -1;
}

/*
 * close_checked — close fd with error reporting; do not retry on EINTR.
 * See pipe_demo.c for rationale.
 */
static int close_checked(int fd)
{
    if (close(fd) < 0) {
        perror("close");
        return -1;
    }
    return 0;
}

int main(void)
{
    static const char response[] = "server 已收到 TCP 请求";
    struct sockaddr_in address;           /* IPv4 socket address struct       */
    char request[BUFFER_SIZE];            /* one framed client request        */
    int listen_fd = -1;                   /* passive / listening socket       */
    int client_fd = -1;                   /* active accepted client socket    */
    int reuse = 1;                        /* boolean for SO_REUSEADDR         */
    int status = EXIT_FAILURE;            /* pessimistic; flip on success     */

    /*
     * ① Create the IPv4 TCP socket and enable SO_REUSEADDR.
     *
     * SO_REUSEADDR allows this server to re-bind port 8888 immediately
     * after a restart, even if the previous instance left the socket in
     * TIME_WAIT state (2*MSL linger, ~60s on Linux).  Without this option,
     * bind() fails with EADDRINUSE for up to two minutes after a killed
     * server — very annoying during teaching demos.
     */
    listen_fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
    if (listen_fd < 0) {
        perror("socket");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    if (setsockopt(listen_fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR,
                   &reuse, sizeof(reuse)) < 0) {
        perror("setsockopt");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ② Bind to 127.0.0.1:8888 and begin listening.
     *
     * We deliberately use 127.0.0.1 (the loopback interface) rather than
     * INADDR_ANY (0.0.0.0) so that only processes running on the SAME
     * machine can connect — this mirrors the AF_UNIX demo's locality and
     * avoids accidentally exposing a teaching socket to the LAN/Internet.
     *
     * htons() converts the port number from host byte order to network
     * (big-endian) byte order as required by all sockaddr_in port fields.
     * inet_pton() validates and packs the dotted-quad string into a
     * 32-bit struct in_addr in network byte order.
     */
    memset(&address, 0, sizeof(address));
    address.sin_family = AF_INET;
    address.sin_port = htons(SERVER_PORT);     /* htons - host-to-network short */
    if (inet_pton(AF_INET, "127.0.0.1", &address.sin_addr) != 1) {
        fprintf(stderr, "inet_pton: 无效的 IPv4 地址\n");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    if (bind(listen_fd, (struct sockaddr *)&address, sizeof(address)) < 0) {
        perror("bind");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    /* Backlog 1 is fine — the demo accepts exactly one client total. */
    if (listen(listen_fd, 1) < 0) {
        perror("listen");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ③ Accept one client connection (blocks until a SYN arrives from
     *    tcp_client on 127.0.0.1:8888 and the 3-way handshake completes).
     */
    do {
        client_fd = accept(listen_fd, NULL, NULL);
    } while (client_fd < 0 && errno == EINTR);
    if (client_fd < 0) {
        perror("accept");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ④ Application protocol: receive one NUL-framed request string,
     *    print to stdout, transmit one NUL-framed reply.
     */
    if (receive_string(client_fd, request, sizeof(request)) < 0) {
        perror("recv");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    if (printf("server 收到：%s\n", request) < 0) {
        perror("printf");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    /* sizeof(response) includes the '\0' that frames the message. */
    if (send_all(client_fd, response, sizeof(response)) < 0) {
        perror("send");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    status = EXIT_SUCCESS;

cleanup:
    if (client_fd >= 0 && close_checked(client_fd) < 0)
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    if (listen_fd >= 0 && close_checked(listen_fd) < 0)
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    return status;
}

#define _POSIX_C_SOURCE 200809L

#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <unistd.h>

/*
 * PROGRAM:     File-backed mmap Reader (regular file + MAP_SHARED)
 * MECHANISM:   POSIX mmap() of a regular file with MAP_SHARED
 * DESCRIPTION: The READER / CONSUMER half of a file-backed shared-memory
 *              demo.  Opens the file /tmp/ipc_mmap_demo.dat (written by
 *              mmap_writer) for reading only with O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW,
 *              confirms via fstat() that it is a regular file of at least
 *              MAP_SIZE bytes, mmap()s the first MAP_SIZE bytes read-only
 *              with MAP_SHARED, scans for a NUL terminator within bounds,
 *              and prints the resulting C string.  As the lifecycle owner
 *              it unlinks the data file before exiting so no stale backing
 *              file is left in /tmp between demo runs.
 * USAGE:       1. Run writer first (creates and populates DATA_FILE):
 *                  ./mmap_writer [optional_message]
 *              2. Immediately after, run THIS reader:
 *                  ./mmap_reader
 * STEPS:       ① open(O_RDONLY) DATA_FILE; error if not present yet
 *              ② fstat() → S_ISREG + st_size >= MAP_SIZE check
 *              ③ mmap(PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED) first MAP_SIZE bytes
 *              ④ memchr() for '\0' inside mapped range → bounded printf
 *              ⑤ munmap + close fd, then unlink() the data file always
 */

#define DATA_FILE "/tmp/ipc_mmap_demo.dat"   /* backing file path, matches writer */
#define MAP_SIZE  4096U                      /* one page, same size as writer    */

int main(void)
{
    int fd = -1;                             /* data file fd                     */
    struct stat file_info;                   /* populated with fstat()            */
    const char *mapping = MAP_FAILED;        /* read-only MAP_SHARED view        */
    const char *terminator;                  /* NUL byte within the mapping       */
    int opened = 0;
    int status = EXIT_FAILURE;

    /*
     * ① Open the file that mmap_writer populated.
     *
     * O_RDONLY    — the reader only reads, so no PROT_WRITE needed.
     * O_CLOEXEC   — don't leak this fd into unrelated child processes.
     * O_NOFOLLOW  — refuse to traverse a symlink; an attacker could have
     *               placed a symlink at DATA_FILE to redirect our open()
     *               into an arbitrary file.
     */
    fd = open(DATA_FILE, O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC | O_NOFOLLOW);
    if (fd == -1) {
        perror("open");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    opened = 1;

    /*
     * ② Validate the file is the right shape before we map anything.
     *
     * S_ISREG rejects FIFOs, devices, sockets, directories, etc. at this
     * path.  The size check guards against an mmap_writer that crashed
     * after open() but before ftruncate(): mapping a zero- or short-sized
     * file and then reading bytes beyond st_size triggers SIGBUS.
     */
    if (fstat(fd, &file_info) == -1) {
        perror("fstat");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    if (!S_ISREG(file_info.st_mode) || file_info.st_size < (off_t)MAP_SIZE) {
        fprintf(stderr, "数据文件不是普通文件或长度不足 %u 字节\n", MAP_SIZE);
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ③ mmap() the first MAP_SIZE bytes read-only.
     *
     * PROT_READ  — only fault in pages for load access (matches O_RDONLY).
     * MAP_SHARED — keep cache-coherent with the underlying file (and with
     *              any other MAP_SHARED mapper).  Even though we won't
     *              write, MAP_SHARED is still the semantically "right"
     *              choice for an IPC-shared view.
     */
    mapping = mmap(NULL, MAP_SIZE, PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED, fd, 0);
    if (mapping == MAP_FAILED) {
        perror("mmap");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ④ Bounded search for the NUL terminator written by mmap_writer.
     *
     * Using memchr() with an explicit length limit guarantees we never
     * walk past the end of the mapping into the next (possibly unmapped)
     * page.  If the writer crashed between memcpy and msync there might
     * be no NUL at all — in that case we error out cleanly instead of
     * letting strlen() SIGSEGV.
     */
    terminator = memchr(mapping, '\0', MAP_SIZE);
    if (terminator == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "映射文件中没有合法的字符串终止符\n");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    printf("读取到 mmap 文件：%.*s\n",
           (int)(terminator - mapping), mapping);
    status = EXIT_SUCCESS;

cleanup:
    if (mapping != MAP_FAILED && munmap((void *)mapping, MAP_SIZE) == -1) {
        perror("munmap");
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    if (fd != -1 && close(fd) == -1) {
        perror("close");
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    /*
     * ⑤ Always unlink DATA_FILE, even on read errors.
     *
     * Like the other reader-side programs in this demo series, the reader
     * owns the final lifecycle step.  If we don't remove the backing
     * file, a repeated `./mmap_writer` run would see EEXIST and waste
     * effort removing it — or worse, a reader crash between runs would
     * leave the file lingering forever in /tmp until reboot.
     */
    if (opened && unlink(DATA_FILE) == -1 && errno != ENOENT) {
        perror("unlink");
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    return status;
}

#define _POSIX_C_SOURCE 200809L

#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <unistd.h>

/*
 * PROGRAM:     File-backed mmap Writer (regular file + MAP_SHARED)
 * MECHANISM:   POSIX mmap() of a regular file with MAP_SHARED
 * DESCRIPTION: The WRITER / CREATOR half of a file-backed shared-memory
 *              demo.  Instead of using POSIX shm_open() or System V shmget(),
 *              this pair relies on mmap() of an ordinary regular file: any
 *              process that opens the same path and maps it with MAP_SHARED
 *              sees the same view of its pages, with the kernel optionally
 *              flushing writes back to disk.  This program creates the file
 *              /tmp/ipc_mmap_demo.dat exclusively (or recreates it if a stale
 *              copy exists), resizes it to MAP_SIZE bytes with ftruncate(),
 *              maps it MAP_SHARED|PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, zero-fills, copies a
 *              NUL-terminated Chinese greeting, and calls msync(MS_SYNC) to
 *              ensure all dirty pages are written to the page cache and disk
 *              before the reader opens it.  On success the file is left in
 *              place for mmap_reader to consume; on failure it is unlinked.
 *              Takes an optional command-line message override.
 * USAGE:       1. Run writer first (creates + populates the data file):
 *                  ./mmap_writer [optional_message]
 *              2. In another terminal, run the reader:
 *                  ./mmap_reader
 *              Reader prints the string then removes the data file.
 * STEPS:       ① Validate message size vs MAP_SIZE
 *              ② open(O_CREAT|O_EXCL) the data file; unlink stale on EEXIST
 *              ③ ftruncate() to MAP_SIZE bytes
 *              ④ mmap(MAP_SHARED | PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE) the full region
 *              ⑤ memset/memcpy the message, msync(MS_SYNC) to disk
 *              ⑥ munmap + close; unlink file only on failure
 */

#define DATA_FILE "/tmp/ipc_mmap_demo.dat"   /* regular file used as backing store */
#define MAP_SIZE  4096U                      /* one 4 KiB page for the demo       */

int main(int argc, char *argv[])
{
    const char *message = argc > 1 ? argv[1] : "来自文件 mmap writer 的消息";
    size_t message_len = strlen(message);
    int fd = -1;                             /* data file descriptor            */
    char *mapping = MAP_FAILED;              /* virtual address of MAP_SHARED view */
    int created = 0;                         /* 1 once open(O_CREAT) succeeds    */
    int status = EXIT_FAILURE;

    if (message_len >= MAP_SIZE) {
        fprintf(stderr, "消息过长，最多允许 %u 字节（需保留结尾空字符）\n",
                MAP_SIZE - 1U);
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    /*
     * ① Create the backing data file.
     *
     * O_CREAT | O_EXCL forces a fresh file; if an older run crashed and
     * left DATA_FILE behind we get EEXIST.  In that case we unlink the
     * stale copy and retry with O_CREAT|O_EXCL again — never reusing an
     * existing file because another process might still have it open with
     * a different size or inconsistent contents.
     *
     * Additional open flags:
     *   O_CLOEXEC   → fd is not inherited across exec() (defense-in-depth)
     *   O_NOFOLLOW  → refuse to open through a symbolic link (prevents an
     *                 attacker from steering us into an arbitrary file)
     * Mode 0600 (owner-only) matches the other IPC demos.
     */
    fd = open(DATA_FILE,
              O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC | O_NOFOLLOW, 0600);
    if (fd == -1 && errno == EEXIST) {
        if (unlink(DATA_FILE) == -1) {
            perror("unlink stale data file");
            goto cleanup;
        }
        fd = open(DATA_FILE,
                  O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC | O_NOFOLLOW, 0600);
    }
    if (fd == -1) {
        perror("open");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    created = 1;

    /*
     * ② Extend the file to exactly MAP_SIZE bytes.
     *
     * A freshly created file has size 0.  mmap() requires pages backed by
     * the file, so any access beyond st_size would trigger SIGBUS.
     * ftruncate() extends the file and allocates the required pages
     * (initially filled with the filesystem's "zero" blocks).
     */
    if (ftruncate(fd, (off_t)MAP_SIZE) == -1) {
        perror("ftruncate");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ③ Map the whole file into our address space.
     *
     * MAP_SHARED is absolutely required for IPC semantics: writes to the
     * mapping update the underlying file AND become visible to every
     * other process mapping the same file with MAP_SHARED.  MAP_PRIVATE
     * would give us copy-on-write pages that only this process sees.
     *
     * The mmap() length is MAP_SIZE (not larger) because ftruncate()
     * guaranteed the file is at least MAP_SIZE bytes long.
     */
    mapping = mmap(NULL, MAP_SIZE, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_SHARED, fd, 0);
    if (mapping == MAP_FAILED) {
        perror("mmap");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ④ Write the message, then msync() to force pages out to disk.
     *
     * With MAP_SHARED, writes become visible to other mappers immediately
     * via the kernel page cache, but "immediately" doesn't mean
     * "persisted to disk" nor "read() on a separate fd sees them" in all
     * VFS implementations.  msync(MS_SYNC) is a portable, explicit
     * flush that blocks until every dirty page inside the mapping range
     * has been written back to the filesystem and acknowledged by it.
     */
    memset(mapping, 0, MAP_SIZE);
    memcpy(mapping, message, message_len + 1U);
    if (msync(mapping, MAP_SIZE, MS_SYNC) == -1) {
        perror("msync");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    printf("已写入 mmap 文件：%s\n", message);
    status = EXIT_SUCCESS;

cleanup:
    if (mapping != MAP_FAILED && munmap(mapping, MAP_SIZE) == -1) {
        perror("munmap");
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    if (fd != -1 && close(fd) == -1) {
        perror("close");
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    /*
     * ⑤ Only clean up the data file on the FAILURE path.
     *
     * On success we deliberately leave DATA_FILE present so the reader
     * can open and mmap() it.  On failure we unlink only if *this* run
     * created the file (tracked by `created`) — never remove a file that
     * existed before our open() call.
     */
    if (status != EXIT_SUCCESS && created &&
        unlink(DATA_FILE) == -1 && errno != ENOENT) {
        perror("unlink data file cleanup");
    }
    return status;
}

#define _POSIX_C_SOURCE 200809L

#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <unistd.h>

/*
 * PROGRAM:     POSIX Shared Memory Reader (shm_open + mmap)
 * MECHANISM:   POSIX shared memory object (shm_open / fstat / mmap)
 * DESCRIPTION: The READER / CONSUMER half of a POSIX shared-memory demo.
 *              Opens the POSIX shared-memory object "/ipc_posix_shm_demo"
 *              (created by posix_shm_writer) read-only, validates that the
 *              object has at least SHM_SIZE bytes of storage, maps the first
 *              SHM_SIZE bytes read-only via mmap(MAP_SHARED), scans for a
 *              NUL terminator within bounds, and prints the resulting string.
 *              As the consumer, this program owns the object's final
 *              lifecycle step: it shm_unlink()s the name before returning so
 *              kernel resources are freed and no stale object survives for
 *              the next demo run.
 * USAGE:       1. First, run the writer (creates the SHM object):
 *                  ./posix_shm_writer [optional_message]
 *              2. Immediately after, run THIS reader:
 *                  ./posix_shm_reader
 * STEPS:       ① shm_open(O_RDONLY) existing object at SHM_NAME
 *              ② fstat() → verify object is large enough for our protocol
 *              ③ mmap(PROT_READ | MAP_SHARED) first SHM_SIZE bytes
 *              ④ memchr() for '\0' within the mapped range, print string
 *              ⑤ munmap + close fd, then shm_unlink() the object name
 */

#define SHM_NAME "/ipc_posix_shm_demo"   /* matches the writer's object name */
#define SHM_SIZE 4096U                   /* same size writer allocated      */

int main(void)
{
    int fd = -1;                          /* SHM object file descriptor     */
    struct stat object_info;              /* populated by fstat()            */
    const char *mapping = MAP_FAILED;     /* read-only view of the region    */
    const char *terminator;               /* points to NUL byte in mapping   */
    int opened = 0;                       /* 1 once shm_open succeeds        */
    int status = EXIT_FAILURE;            /* pessimistic default             */

    /*
     * ① Open existing SHM object read-only.
     *
     * No O_CREAT flag: if the writer hasn't run yet (or already unlinked
     * the object after itself), shm_open fails with ENOENT and the user
     * gets a clear diagnostic via perror("shm_open").
     */
    fd = shm_open(SHM_NAME, O_RDONLY, 0);
    if (fd == -1) {
        perror("shm_open");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    opened = 1;

    /*
     * ② Validate the object is actually big enough.
     *
     * A malicious or buggy writer could create a POSIX SHM object at the
     * same name but with a smaller ftruncate() call.  Mapping such an
     * undersized object and then reading SHM_SIZE bytes would SIGBUS the
     * reader the moment it accesses any byte beyond st_size.  fstat()
     * lets us catch that before we touch any mapping.
     */
    if (fstat(fd, &object_info) == -1) {
        perror("fstat");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    if (object_info.st_size < (off_t)SHM_SIZE) {
        fprintf(stderr, "POSIX 共享内存对象长度不足 %u 字节\n", SHM_SIZE);
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ③ Establish a read-only MAP_SHARED view of the object.
     *
     * MAP_SHARED (rather than MAP_PRIVATE) is still required even though
     * we are reading: MAP_PRIVATE would perform copy-on-write for the
     * page tables which is wasteful, and more importantly some
     * architectures only guarantee cache coherency with MAP_SHARED when
     * the writer is also using MAP_SHARED (both use consistent flags
     * across the pair in this demo).
     */
    mapping = mmap(NULL, SHM_SIZE, PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED, fd, 0);
    if (mapping == MAP_FAILED) {
        perror("mmap");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ④ Look for a NUL terminator strictly within the SHM_SIZE region.
     *
     * memchr() limits the scan to the bytes we actually mapped — never
     * strlen() the mapping directly: a writer that failed to write a
     * terminator (or deliberately omitted one) would cause strlen to
     * walk off the end of the page into unmapped memory and SIGSEGV.
     */
    terminator = memchr(mapping, '\0', SHM_SIZE);
    if (terminator == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "共享内存中没有合法的字符串终止符\n");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    printf("读取到 POSIX 共享内存：%.*s\n",
           (int)(terminator - mapping), mapping);
    status = EXIT_SUCCESS;

cleanup:
    if (mapping != MAP_FAILED && munmap((void *)mapping, SHM_SIZE) == -1) {
        perror("munmap");
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    if (fd != -1 && close(fd) == -1) {
        perror("close");
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    /*
     * ⑤ Reader is the lifecycle owner: always unlink the name so the
     *    kernel can release the object once all mappings are torn down.
     *    We do this even if we hit a read-path error — a failed demo run
     *    should still not leak a named kernel object.  ENOENT (someone
     *    else already unlinked it) is not considered an error.
     */
    if (opened && shm_unlink(SHM_NAME) == -1 && errno != ENOENT) {
        perror("shm_unlink");
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    return status;
}

#define _POSIX_C_SOURCE 200809L

#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <unistd.h>

/*
 * PROGRAM:     POSIX Shared Memory Writer (shm_open + mmap)
 * MECHANISM:   POSIX shared memory object (shm_open / ftruncate / mmap)
 * DESCRIPTION: The WRITER / CREATOR half of a POSIX shared-memory demo.
 *              Creates a new POSIX shared-memory object named
 *              "/ipc_posix_shm_demo" via shm_open(O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_RDWR),
 *              resizes it to SHM_SIZE bytes with ftruncate(), mmaps it into
 *              the address space with MAP_SHARED (required so writes become
 *              visible to other processes mapping the same object), and
 *              writes a NUL-terminated Chinese greeting.  On success the
 *              object is left in place for posix_shm_reader to open and
 *              read; on failure it is unlinked immediately to avoid leaks.
 *              Accepts an optional command-line argument to override the
 *              default message.
 * USAGE:       1. Compile and run this writer first (it creates the SHM):
 *                  ./posix_shm_writer [optional_message]
 *              2. In another terminal, run the reader:
 *                  ./posix_shm_reader
 *              Reader unlinks the POSIX SHM object after consuming it.
 * STEPS:       ① Validate message length
 *              ② shm_open(O_CREAT|O_EXCL); remove stale object on EEXIST
 *              ③ ftruncate() to SHM_SIZE (new objects start at zero length)
 *              ④ mmap(MAP_SHARED | PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE) the full region
 *              ⑤ Zero fill, copy message + NUL into the mapping
 *              ⑥ munmap() + close() fd; unlink only if we failed
 */

#define SHM_NAME "/ipc_posix_shm_demo"   /* POSIX SHM name (starts with "/") */
#define SHM_SIZE 4096U                   /* one 4 KiB page, plenty for demo */

int main(int argc, char *argv[])
{
    const char *message = argc > 1 ? argv[1] : "来自 POSIX 共享内存 writer 的消息";
    size_t message_len = strlen(message);
    int fd = -1;                          /* SHM object file descriptor     */
    char *mapping = MAP_FAILED;           /* virtual address of our mapping  */
    int created = 0;                      /* 1 once shm_open(O_CREAT) wins   */
    int status = EXIT_FAILURE;            /* pessimistic until proven OK     */

    /*
     * ① The shared region must hold the message bytes AND a trailing NUL,
     *    so reject anything longer than SHM_SIZE - 1 up front.
     */
    if (message_len >= SHM_SIZE) {
        fprintf(stderr, "消息过长，最多允许 %u 字节（需保留结尾空字符）\n",
                SHM_SIZE - 1U);
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    /*
     * ② Create the POSIX shared-memory object exclusively.
     *
     * shm_open() returns a file descriptor that refers to an anonymous,
     * kernel-backed object identified by a slash-prefixed name.  The
     * O_CREAT|O_EXCL pair ensures we are the sole creator — if another
     * process/previous crashed run left the object behind (EEXIST), we
     * remove it with shm_unlink() and retry so the demo always starts
     * with a clean, freshly-sized region.
     *
     * Mode 0600 (owner read/write only) mirrors the permission style used
     * for FIFO/SysV demos — no world access to a teaching IPC channel.
     */
    fd = shm_open(SHM_NAME, O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_RDWR, 0600);
    if (fd == -1 && errno == EEXIST) {
        /* Stale object from a prior crashed writer → remove and recreate. */
        if (shm_unlink(SHM_NAME) == -1) {
            perror("shm_unlink stale object");
            goto cleanup;
        }
        fd = shm_open(SHM_NAME, O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_RDWR, 0600);
    }
    if (fd == -1) {
        perror("shm_open");
        goto cleanup;
    }
    created = 1;

    /*
     * ③ Resize the object to SHM_SIZE bytes.
     *
     * A freshly created POSIX SHM object always has length 0 — mapping it
     * would produce a SIGBUS on any access because there are no pages
     * backing the addresses.  ftruncate() allocates storage and defines
     * how far mmap()'d accesses remain valid.
     */
    if (ftruncate(fd, (off_t)SHM_SIZE) == -1) {
        perror("ftruncate");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ④ Map the object into our virtual address space.
     *
     * MAP_SHARED is CRITICAL for IPC: any byte we write to the mapping is
     * immediately (subject to cache coherency) visible to every other
     * process that also maps the same object with MAP_SHARED.  If we
     * mistakenly used MAP_PRIVATE the kernel would give us a
     * copy-on-write mapping — our writes would only modify our own
     * private pages and the reader would never see them.
     */
    mapping = mmap(NULL, SHM_SIZE, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_SHARED, fd, 0);
    if (mapping == MAP_FAILED) {
        perror("mmap");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    /*
     * ⑤ Populate the region: zero the whole page, copy the message plus
     *    NUL terminator.  The reader scans for '\0' as a string boundary
     *    and refuses to read beyond SHM_SIZE even if the terminator is
     *    missing (protects against a malicious/compromised writer).
     */
    memset(mapping, 0, SHM_SIZE);
    memcpy(mapping, message, message_len + 1U);
    printf("已写入 POSIX 共享内存：%s\n", message);
    status = EXIT_SUCCESS;

cleanup:
    if (mapping != MAP_FAILED && munmap(mapping, SHM_SIZE) == -1) {
        perror("munmap");
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    if (fd != -1 && close(fd) == -1) {
        perror("close");
        status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    /*
     * ⑥ Lifecycle rule: on SUCCESS we deliberately leave the object
     *    present so posix_shm_reader can open and consume it.  On any
     *    failure path we unlink it to avoid leaking a kernel object
     *    (POSIX shared memory objects have kernel persistence — they
     *    survive the creating process until shm_unlink()ed).
     */
    if (status != EXIT_SUCCESS && created && shm_unlink(SHM_NAME) == -1 &&
        errno != ENOENT) {
        perror("shm_unlink cleanup");
    }
    return status;
}

#include <errno.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <sys/wait.h>
